slot.brief: Form the differential equation of a family y = Ae^{kx} + B (or similar) by eliminating arbitrary constants

stem: The family of curves $y=Ae^{3x}+B$, where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants, has differential equation
working:
$y'=3Ae^{3x}$; $y''=9Ae^{3x}=3y'$. Hence $y''-3y'=0$.

Independent check: Differentiate: y'=3Ae^{3x}, y''=9Ae^{3x}. Thus y''-3y'=0.
solution:
Differentiating $y=Ae^{3x}+B$ gives
$$y'=3Ae^{3x},\qquad y''=9Ae^{3x}=3y'.$$
Hence the required differential equation is $y''-3y'=0$.
